sources.title: D. Cline, Variational Principles in Classical Mechanics (2nd edition, University of Rochester River Campus Libraries, open textbook, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0), Chapter 15 'Advanced Hamiltonian Mechanics', Sections 15.1-15.5 and 15.7-15.8; read from the fetched compilation
sources.locator: Chapter 15, Sections 15.2 (Poisson bracket representation), 15.3 (canonical transformations), 15.4 (Hamilton-Jacobi theory), 15.5 (action-angle variables), 15.7 (symplectic representation); 15.1, 15.6 and 15.8 inspected for scope

contents.name: 15.2 Poisson bracket representation of Hamiltonian mechanics
contents.support: The coordinate Poisson-bracket formula and the relation of the bracket to the canonical equations; used as the second treatment behind the choice-free local proposition.

contents.name: 15.3 Canonical transformations in Hamiltonian mechanics
contents.support: The four kinds of generating function, the relations p = dS_1/dq and P = -dS_1/dQ, and the local character of the construction.

contents.name: 15.3 Canonical transformations in Hamiltonian mechanics (symplectic condition)
contents.support: The chapter's statement that canonicity is equivalent to preservation of the symplectic structure, which the local proposition turns into the matrix test.

contents.name: 15.4 Hamilton-Jacobi theory
contents.support: The Hamilton-Jacobi equation, Jacobi's complete integral, and the use of the constants dS/dalpha; the local theorem re-derives the characteristics, the constants and the canonical labels.

contents.name: 15.5 Action-angle variables
contents.support: The period conventions for action-angle variables; used only for the period-one to radian conversion corollary.

contents.name: 15.5 Action-angle variables (integrable systems)
contents.support: The chapter's presentation of action-angle variables for integrable systems; the local theorem's complete proof follows the cited treatments and repairs the published two-form gap.

contents.name: 15.6 Canonical perturbation theory
contents.reason: Canonical perturbation series and resonance analysis are the subject of the approximation and KAM layers of this collection, not of the canonical-methods page.

contents.name: 15.7 Symplectic representation
contents.support: The antisymmetric matrix representation of the symplectic form and of canonical linear maps, absorbed into the matrix test of the local proposition.

contents.name: 15.8 Comparison of the Lagrangian and Hamiltonian formulations
contents.reason: A comparison chapter for pedagogy; the local page needs no statement from it and the Legendre comparison is authored on the variations and dynamics pages.

sources.title: D. Tong, Classical Dynamics (University of Cambridge Part II Mathematical Tripos), Chapter 4 'The Hamiltonian Formalism', printed pages 80-133
sources.locator: Sections 4.1 (Hamilton's equations, printed pages 80-88), 4.2 (Liouville's theorem, 88-92), 4.3 (Poisson brackets, 93-99), 4.4 (canonical transformations and generating functions, 100-105), 4.5 (action-angle variables, 105-112), 4.6 (adiabatic invariants, 113-121, inspected for scope), 4.7 (the Hamilton-Jacobi equation, 121-126), 4.8 (quantum mechanics, 126-133, inspected for scope)

contents.name: 4.1 Hamilton's equations (including 4.1.1 the Legendre transform and 4.1.5 the principle of least action)
contents.support: The derivation of Hamilton's equations from the symplectic contraction and the canonical-coordinate form of the field; used as the first treatment behind the local proposition.

contents.name: 4.2 Liouville's theorem
contents.support: The preservation of phase-space volume by Hamiltonian flows, which the local corollary obtains from the unit determinant of the flow derivative and the change-of-variables theorem.

contents.name: 4.3 Poisson brackets
contents.support: The algebraic properties of the Poisson bracket (bilinearity, antisymmetry, Leibniz); the local page cites the published bracket-identity items rather than re-proving them.

contents.name: 4.4 Canonical transformations (4.4.1 infinitesimal transformations, 4.4.3 generating functions)
contents.support: The condition M^T J M = J for a canonical transformation and the local/global discussion of generating functions.

contents.name: 4.4.3 Generating functions
contents.support: The time-dependent generating function and the shift K = H + dS/dt of the Hamiltonian.

contents.name: 4.5 Action-angle variables (4.5.2 integrable systems, 4.5.3 one-dimensional systems, 4.5.4 Kepler)
contents.support: The construction of action-angle variables for integrable systems and the cylinder/angle-variable examples; the local theorem is proved from the cited symplectic sources and the published torus suppliers.

contents.name: 4.5 Action-angle variables (period conventions)
contents.support: The angle variable on the cylinder and the shift symmetry, used as the concrete obstruction example for global generating functions.

contents.name: 4.6 Adiabatic invariants
contents.reason: Adiabatic invariance, averaging and drift estimates are the subject of the approximation layer (E8); none of its content is used on this page.

contents.name: 4.7 The Hamilton-Jacobi equation (including 4.7.1 action and angles from Hamilton-Jacobi)
contents.support: The characteristic equations q-dot = H_p with p = W_q, the verification of Hamilton's second equation, and the canonical coordinates (alpha, beta) with alpha = dW/dbeta.

contents.name: 4.8 Quantum mechanics
contents.reason: Quantum-mechanical and path-integral bridges require an independent quantum framework with its own domains and limits, deferred beyond this design.

sources.title: Ana Cannas da Silva, Lectures on Symplectic Geometry, revised January 2006, Lectures 1-2 and Lecture 18
sources.locator: Symplectic forms and canonical forms on R^{2n} (Lecture 1, pp. 9-12), and Lecture 18 'Hamiltonian Vector Fields', Definition 18.10, Lemma 18.11 and Theorem 18.12 (Arnold-Liouville), pp. 108-111

contents.name: Canonical form on T*X and the standard symplectic form on R^{2n} (Lecture 1, pp. 9-12)
contents.support: The coordinate model lambda = sum p_i dq^i, omega = sum dq^i wedge dp_i and its nondegeneracy, which the local definition and lemma instantiate choice-free on a phase domain.

contents.name: Definition 18.10 (completely integrable system)
contents.support: Involution of n independent integrals as the integrability hypothesis; the local theorem states the same hypothesis and consumes the published definition.

contents.name: Lemma 18.11 (complete flows on a level give a homogeneous-space structure)
contents.support: Completeness of the commuting fields on the fibre and the resulting transitive action; the local theorem obtains completeness from the published compact-manifold supplier.

contents.name: Theorem 18.12 (Arnold-Liouville), parts (a) and (b)
contents.support: Angle coordinates in which the flows are linear and complementary action coordinates forming a Darboux chart. Source limitation recorded: the printed proof sketches part (a) and refers part (b) to other references; the local theorem's complete proof uses the supplementing sources below.

sources.title: Eckhard Meinrenken, Symplectic Geometry (Fall 2024 lecture notes), Chapter 6, sections 6.1-6.3

contents.name: Propositions 6.10, 6.12 and 6.15 (complete Lagrangian submersions, transitive cotangent action, Lagrangian period-lattice bundle)
contents.support: The action map, the period-lattice submanifold Lambda and the transverse/Lagrangian properties used in the local construction.

contents.name: Theorem 6.21 (Liouville-Arnold)
contents.support: The full local action-angle statement with the affine torus structure and linear flow, used as the primary complete treatment for part (b).

contents.name: Warnings and examples in 6.1-6.3 (lattice need not be locally trivial; sections and Lagrangian sections)
contents.support: The notes' caution that period lattices need not be locally trivial and that a section is symplectic only when Lagrangian; the scope remark records the saturated-properness hypotheses under which the local construction is made.

sources.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition, Chapter 17 (Integration on Manifolds: the Poincare lemma)

contents.name: Theorem 17.14 (Poincare lemma for closed forms on star-shaped domains)
contents.support: Closed smooth k-forms on star-shaped open domains are exact, with the explicit radial primitive obtained from the homotopy formula.

contents.name: Chapter 17 pullback and exterior-derivative calculus
contents.support: The pullback/evaluation calculus used throughout the canonical-map and generating-function items.

sources.title: Nigel Hitchin, Differentiable Manifolds (2014), the Poincare lemma and radial contraction
sources.locator: The Poincare lemma chapter and the explicit radial-contraction formula

contents.name: Poincare lemma / radial contraction formula
contents.support: An independent exposition of the radial primitive formula whose k=2 instance the local lemma records with its explicit coefficient verification.
